drafts.title: California Powerwalls as a paycheck
drafts.angle: Home batteries paid to help the grid during a heatwave
bullets: About 69,000 CA Powerwalls discharged together Sep 9 evening peak
Owners keep backup reserve; programs pay for peak export
Not in CA? Ask your utility for VPP / on-bill battery
drafts.body:
Skip the culture war. Look at the meter.

Tesla Energy said roughly 69,000 California Powerwall households discharged together during the Sep 9 evening peak. Combined output topped 500 MW.

Owners keep a reserve for outages. Programs pay you to export when the grid is stressed. A home battery can be storm backup and a seasonal paycheck.

Not in California? Ask your utility for VPP / Power Partner / on-bill battery. Bring the 500 MW headline as proof.

drafts.title: Suniva $835M South Carolina solar cells
drafts.angle: US cell factory → future panel price independence
bullets: Suniva closed $835M for Laurens County SC cell plant
With Georgia plant ~5.5 GW US cell capacity
Ask installer what’s domestic vs import; get warranty entity in writing
drafts.body:
Solar on your roof is only as independent as the supply chain behind it.

Suniva closed $835M for a Laurens County, SC cell plant: about 4.5 GW, about 564 jobs, late 2027 target. With Georgia, about 5.5 GW US cell capacity.

Won’t cut your quote next Tuesday. Over a few cycles it helps stabilize hardware when tariffs and shipping swing.

drafts.title: PSE&G $5k home battery + 0% on-bill
drafts.angle: Utility cash after federal battery credit closed
bullets: Federal residential battery credit closed for 2026 installs
Up to $25,000 remaining at 0% on the utility bill
Ask your utility for the local equivalent by name
drafts.body:
Federal residential battery credit is closed for 2026 installs. Utilities didn’t get the memo.

PSE&G GridSmart: $5,000 toward a new home battery plus up to $25,000 at 0% on the bill. No solar required. They can call peak events; you keep the hardware.

Ask your utility for the local equivalent. Backup reserve first.

drafts.title: Rivian Chicago robotaxi tests
drafts.angle: Future ride cost + cheaper autonomy on family EVs
bullets: Rivian collecting data in SF, Miami, Chicago (Uber partnership)
RAP1 chip testing wrapping in about 6 weeks
Household stake: ride cost in big cities + cheaper hardware packages
drafts.body:
Robotaxi talk usually floats above the kitchen table. This update has a city name and a clock.

Rivian is collecting robotaxi data in San Francisco, Miami, and Chicago. Custom RAP1 chip testing is wrapping soon.

Household stake: future ride cost in big cities, and cheaper autonomy hardware on family EVs. Supervised help now; empty seats later.

drafts.title: Bidirectional EV pilots up to ~$3,200/yr
drafts.angle: EV paycheck from pilots — not a promise
bullets: Some CA pilots: up to about $3,200 per vehicle per year
Equipment help up to about $13,800 in some lanes
Ask: approved vehicle/charger, who pays hardware, reserve for tomorrow’s drive
drafts.body:
Your car battery can be more than a commute tank.

Some California pilots talk up to about $3,200 per vehicle per year exporting EV energy, plus equipment help in some programs. Not guaranteed income.

Ask: Is my vehicle and charger approved? Who pays for the gear? What reserve do I keep for tomorrow morning?
